mainTopic: סמיכה: the three times the תורה says קרבנו, whether a יורש does סמיכה and can make a תמורה, and who is left out of סמיכה
overview: The גמרא first explains that each of the three times the תורה says קרבנו teaches its own rule about סמיכה. It then turns to the משנה's rule that a יורש (heir) does סמיכה and can make a תמורה. רב חנניה recites a ברייתא that says the opposite. רבא shows that this ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who argues with the תנא קמא. The גמרא then gives each side's source. רבי יהודה learns from קרבנו that an heir does not do סמיכה, and from that he also excludes the heir from תמורה. The רבנן learn from ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ that an heir can make a תמורה, and from that they include him in סמיכה. Each side then explains how it uses the other side's verse, and where a woman's ability to make a תמורה comes from. A new משנה then lists who does not do סמיכה, calls סמיכה ״שְׁיָרֵי מִצְוָה״, and explains how it is done. The גמרא starts by asking why a blind person is left out, and it brings two sources from two אמוראים.

steps.title: Why does the תורה need these verses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the three verses that say קרבנו are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the three verses that say קרבנו are for. This question sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion showed that the repeated word קרבנו is not needed to block a קל וחומר. So now each extra קרבנו needs its own job, or it looks like the תורה wasted words.

keyTerms.meaning: verses (from the תורה)
why do I need it? What does it teach?

phrases.english: Why do I need the verses?
phrases.notes: He means the three times the תורה says קרבנו about placing hands on a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion, which showed the verses are not needed to block a קל וחומר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of the three times קרבנו appears teaches about סמיכה.

steps.title: Each 'his offering' teaches a different rule
steps.stepSummary: One קרבנו excludes another person's קרבן, one excludes a גוי's קרבן, and one includes all the partners who own a קרבן in סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His offering' means not his friend's offering. 'His offering' means not a non-Jew's offering. 'His offering' comes to include all the owners of an offering in placing hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each of the three times the word קרבנו appears teaches its own rule about סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of the three verses limit סמיכה: you do it only on your own קרבן, not on another Jew's and not on a גוי's. The third verse widens it: if several people own one animal together, every one of them does סמיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: his offering
placing one's hands on the animal before it is offered
the owners of an offering
to include (to add a case to the rule)

steps.whatToRemember: Three times קרבנו: (1) not another person's קרבן, (2) not a גוי's קרבן, (3) all partners in a קרבן do סמיכה.

phrases.english: 'His offering' — and not the offering of his fellow;
'His offering' — and not the offering of a non-Jew;
'His offering' — to include all the owners of an offering in placing hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each קרבנו teaches a separate rule: not another person's קרבן, not a גוי's, and all partners do סמיכה.

steps.title: The משנה: an heir places hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a יורש does סמיכה, opening a new topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: The heir places hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה: an heir does סמיכה on a קרבן he inherited. This opens the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner of a קרבן dies before it is offered, the משנה treats his heir as the new owner. So the heir does סמיכה, just as the original owner would have.

keyTerms.meaning: heir, the one who inherits
places his hands (does סמיכה)

phrases.english: The heir places hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יורש does סמיכה on a קרבן he inherited.

steps.title: רב חנניה's ברייתא: an heir does not place hands
steps.stepSummary: רב חנניה recites a ברייתא before רבא: a יורש does not do סמיכה and cannot make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנניה taught before רבא: An heir does not place hands, and an heir cannot make a substitution.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנניה recites a teaching in front of רבא that says the opposite of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא says the heir is not treated as the full owner for סמיכה or for תמורה. That clashes with the משנה, and the next step points out the clash.

keyTerms.meaning: in front of him, in his presence
makes a תמורה (tries to swap another animal for the קרבן)
swapping a regular animal for a קרבן; both animals end up holy

steps.confusionAlert: Making a תמורה is forbidden. But if the owner does it, it takes effect: the new animal also becomes holy. So 'he can make a תמורה' means it works, not that he is allowed to.

phrases.english: Rav Chananya taught before Rava:
An heir does not place hands,
an heir cannot make a substitution.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יורש does not do סמיכה and cannot make a תמורה.

steps.title: רבא objects: the משנה says the heir does place hands
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the ברייתא from the משנה, which says a יורש does סמיכה, brings the נסכים, and can make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn: The heir places hands, brings its libations, and can make a substitution?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב חנניה: your ברייתא goes against our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says yes on exactly the two points where the ברייתא says no: סמיכה and תמורה. A ברייתא normally should not contradict the משנה, so רבא asks how this can be.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't we learn (in the משנה)? Used to raise a contradiction
its נסכים: the wine and flour offerings that come with the animal

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the mishnah:
The heir places hands, and brings its libations,
and can make a substitution.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא of step 4 using the משנה of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חנניה's ברייתא, which says a יורש does not do סמיכה or make a תמורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה clearly says a יורש does both, so the ברייתא contradicts it.

steps.title: Should I reverse the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: רב חנניה offers to reverse his ברייתא so that it matches the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Should I reverse it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנניה asks רבא whether he should flip the wording of his ברייתא to agree with the משנה. This sets up רבא's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His idea is that the ברייתא was simply learned the wrong way around. Reversing it would make the contradiction go away.

keyTerms.meaning: reverse it, flip the wording

phrases.english: He said to him: Should I reverse it?
phrases.notes: He is offering to change his ברייתא to say 'the heir does place hands'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבא's challenge by offering to fix the wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether to correct the ברייתא by reversing its wording.

steps.title: רבא: no, the teaching follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says not to reverse it. The teaching has a real author, רבי יהודה, so it can stay as it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. Whose view is this teaching? It is רבי יהודה's.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that the ברייתא should not be changed, because it follows the view of a specific תנא, רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not a mistake. It is a real opinion that disagrees with the משנה's view. Two תנאים can argue, so the ברייתא and the משנה can both be correct versions of different opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: whose is it? Who is the author?
the teaching (here, the one being identified)

steps.confusionAlert: From the ברייתא in the next step, רבי יהודה holds an heir does NOT place hands. So the teaching that matches him is רב חנניה's ברייתא, not the משנה, which follows the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
whose is the teaching? It is Rabbi Yehuda's,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לָא מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reversal offered in step 6 and resolves the challenge of step 5 another way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the two sources to different תנאים who argue.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא contradicts the משנה, so it must be wrong and needs reversing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and the משנה follows the תנא קמא, who argues with him.

steps.title: Proof: a ברייתא where רבי יהודה disagrees
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows a real argument: the תנא קמא says a יורש does סמיכה and can make a תמורה, and רבי יהודה says he does neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: An heir places hands, an heir can make a substitution. רבי יהודה says: An heir does not place hands, an heir cannot make a substitution.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his point by quoting a ברייתא where this exact argument appears by name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion matches the משנה. רבי יהודה's opinion matches רב חנניה's ברייתא word for word. So both sources are correct, each following a different תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: the first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא (like our משנה): a יורש does סמיכה and can make a תמורה. רבי יהודה (like רב חנניה's ברייתא): a יורש does neither.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
An heir places hands, an heir can make a substitution.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ, יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ מֵימֵר.
phrases.english: An heir does not place hands, an heir cannot make a substitution.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רב חנניה's ברייתא is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording an argument between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה about a יורש.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי יהודה's view that an heir does no סמיכה and cannot make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know there is a real argument, the גמרא asks why רבי יהודה holds his view. This line sets up the next step, which gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 only showed that רבי יהודה disagrees with the תנא קמא. Now the גמרא wants the source in the פסוקים for his position.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view of רבי יהודה that was shown in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for רבי יהודה's view that a יורש does no סמיכה and makes no תמורה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns from ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ and compares the start of הקדש to its end
steps.stepSummary: ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ means your own offering, not your father's, so an heir does no סמיכה. Since an heir has no part in the end of הקדש (סמיכה), he also has no part in its start (תמורה).
steps.simpleTranslation: The word ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ (his offering) means his own offering, not his father's. He also learns the beginning of הקדש from the end of הקדש. At the end of הקדש, an heir does not do סמיכה. So at the beginning of הקדש, an heir cannot make a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's two-part reasoning. First, a פסוק shows an heir does no סמיכה. Then he extends that rule to תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ limits סמיכה to the person whose offering it really is, not an heir. רבי יהודה then links תמורה (making holiness happen) to סמיכה (the last step before שחיטה). Whatever applies to one applies to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: "His offering", the word in the סמיכה פסוקים
The start of holiness, here meaning תמורה
The end stage of the offering, here meaning סמיכה
An heir
Leans his hands on the animal (does סמיכה)
Makes a תמורה (substitutes another animal)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two stages. תמורה is called the "start" because it makes a new animal holy. סמיכה is the "end" because it happens right before the animal is slaughtered.

phrases.english: "His offering", and not his father's offering,
and he learns the beginning of consecration from the end of consecration:

phrases.aramaic: מָה סוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ – יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ,
phrases.english: just as at the end of consecration, an heir does not lean his hands,

phrases.aramaic: אַף תְּחִילַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ – יוֹרֵשׁ אֵינוֹ מֵימֵר.
phrases.english: so too at the beginning of consecration, an heir cannot make a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ excludes the father's offering from סמיכה, and תמורה is learned from סמיכה, so an heir does neither.

steps.title: The רבנן learn from ״הָמֵר יָמִיר″ and compare the end of הקדש to its start
steps.stepSummary: The doubled words ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ include an heir in תמורה. Since an heir can make a תמורה, he also does סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן learn from ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ ("he shall surely substitute") that an heir is included. They learn the end of הקדש from the beginning of הקדש. At the beginning of הקדש, an heir can make a תמורה. So at the end of הקדש, an heir does סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the source for the רבנן. They use the same comparison as רבי יהודה, but in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן start from תמורה, where a doubled word in the פסוק includes the heir. Then they carry that rule over to סמיכה. Both sides agree the two stages go together. They only disagree about which פסוק sets the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: "He shall surely substitute", a doubled phrase (ויקרא 27:10)
To include
Learns (one law from another)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides link סמיכה and תמורה together. רבי יהודה starts from סמיכה (heir excluded). The רבנן start from תמורה (heir included).

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: "He shall surely substitute", to include the heir,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10. The doubled verb is read as adding someone extra, here the heir.

phrases.english: and they learn the end of consecration from the beginning of consecration:
just as at the beginning of consecration, an heir can make a substitute,
so too at the end of consecration, an heir leans his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side's source, parallel to רבי יהודה's in Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ includes the heir in תמורה, and סמיכה is learned from תמורה.

steps.title: How do the רבנן use the word ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״?
steps.stepSummary: Since the רבנן do not use ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ to exclude an heir, the גמרא asks what they learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this word ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from the word that רבי יהודה used. This sets up the next step, which explains their use of each ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word in the תורה is not extra. If the רבנן reject רבי יהודה's reading, they must use ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it? What do they learn from it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this "his offering",
what do they do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on Step 11 by asking how the רבנן handle רבי יהודה's source from Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״, since they do not use it to exclude the heir.

steps.title: The רבנן use each of the three ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ for something else
steps.stepSummary: One ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ excludes a גוי's offering. One excludes a friend's offering. One includes all partners in an offering in סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״: not a גוי's offering. ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״: not his friend's offering. ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״: to include all the owners of an offering in סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the word appears three times, and the רבנן use up all three. That leaves none to exclude an heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two uses exclude people who are not the owner: a גוי and a friend. The third use includes every partner in a shared offering, so each one must do סמיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew
His friend, another person
The owners (partners) of an offering

phrases.english: "His offering", and not the offering of a gentile,
"His offering", and not the offering of his friend,
"His offering", to include all owners of an offering in leaning hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ teach: not a גוי, not a friend, and include all partners.

steps.title: First answer: רבי יהודה does not hold of including partners
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה does not learn that all partners need סמיכה. So one ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ is free to exclude the heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה does not hold that a ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ is needed to include all owners of an offering in סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a hidden question: if all three uses are needed, how can רבי יהודה use one for the heir? Its first answer is that he does not learn the rule about partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה skips the third use (partners). That frees up a ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״, which he uses to exclude the father's offering.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold of it

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל בַּעֲלֵי קׇרְבָּן לִסְמִיכָה
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, to include all owners of an offering in leaning hands,
he does not hold of it,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל בַּעֲלֵי קׇרְבָּן לִסְמִיכָה – לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 13 uses up all three ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״, this step explains where רבי יהודה finds a spare one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ are needed, leaving רבי יהודה no source for excluding the heir.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה does not hold of including partners, so one ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ is free.

steps.title: Second answer: one ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ covers both the גוי and the friend
steps.stepSummary: Even if רבי יהודה does include partners, he learns both the גוי and the friend from one ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״. That leaves two more: one for the heir and one for partners.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, even if he does hold of it, the גוי and the friend both come from one פסוק. So two פסוקים are left over for him. One teaches ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״, not his father's offering. The other includes all owners of an offering in סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to answer for רבי יהודה. He can keep the rule about partners and still have a ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ to exclude the heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן spend two uses on the גוי and the friend. רבי יהודה learns both from one. That saves a ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״, which he uses to exclude the heir.

keyTerms.meaning: Or alternatively
It comes out (is learned from)
Are left over
Two פסוקים (here, two times the word appears)
The other one

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use the extra words in the פסוקים fully. They only differ in how they divide the three ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״. That difference is what decides whether an heir does סמיכה.

phrases.english: And alternatively, if he does hold of it,
a gentile and his friend are both derived from one verse.
Two verses are left over for him:
one, "his offering" and not his father's offering,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִידַּךְ – לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל בַּעֲלֵי קׇרְבָּן לִסְמִיכָה.
phrases.english: and the other, to include all owners of an offering in leaning hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, in place of Step 14, explaining how רבי יהודה has a spare ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי יהודה includes partners, he has no spare ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״ for the heir.
steps.terutzMaskana: He learns the גוי and the friend from one ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״, which frees one for the heir and one for partners.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה's view is fully grounded in the פסוקים either way.

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה learn from the doubled words?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that an heir cannot make a תמורה, so he cannot use ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ to include an heir. The גמרא asks what he uses those doubled words for.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה, what does he do with the doubled words ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה learns from ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 the רבנן used the doubled words to include an heir in תמורה. רבי יהודה holds that an heir cannot make a תמורה (step 10), so he cannot use the words for that. The גמרא wants to know what the doubled words teach in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Doubled verb form, 'he shall surely substitute.' The doubling is expounded to add a teaching.
'What does he do with it?' The גמרא is asking what a sage learns from a word.

phrases.english: And רבי יהודה,
this phrase "he shall surely substitute"
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַאי ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining how רבי יהודה uses ״קׇרְבָּנוֹ״, the גמרא now asks how he uses the other verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יהודה learns from the doubled words ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״

steps.title: He uses it to include a woman in תמורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ to teach that a woman can make a תמורה. A ברייתא supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to include a woman. As a ברייתא teaches: the whole passage speaks only in the masculine, so how do we come to include a woman? The verse says ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה uses the doubled words to include a woman in the law of תמורה. It brings a ברייתא that says exactly this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's passage on תמורה uses only masculine language. Without a special source, we might think only a man can make a תמורה. The ברייתא says the doubled words add a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: To include, meaning to add a case to a law.
Masculine language
'The verse says,' introducing the Torah source for a teaching.

phrases.english: He needs it to include a woman,
as it is taught:
Since the entire passage
speaks only in masculine language,
how do we end up including a woman?
The verse says "he shall surely substitute."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הָאִשָּׁה, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה uses ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ to teach that a woman can make a תמורה, as the ברייתא states.

steps.title: The רבנן learn the woman from the word ״וְאִם״
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן used the doubled words for the heir, so they need another source for the woman. They learn her from ״וְאִם״. רבי יהודה does not expound that word, so he needs the doubled words for the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן expound the woman from ״וְאִם״. And רבי יהודה does not expound ״וְאִם״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where the רבנן learn that a woman can make a תמורה. It also explains why רבי יהודה cannot learn it from the same place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a hidden question here: the רבנן used ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ for the heir, so what is their source for the woman? They take it from the extra ״וְ״ of ״וְאִם״. רבי יהודה finds no extra teaching in ״וְאִם״, so he must use ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ for the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: They expound, meaning they draw a teaching from a word.
'And if.' The extra ״וְ״ (and) can be read as adding a case.

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that a woman can make a תמורה. They only disagree about the source. The רבנן use ״וְאִם״ for the woman and ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ for the heir. רבי יהודה uses ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ for the woman and does not include the heir.

phrases.english: And the רבנן expound it from "and if,"
phrases.notes: The פסוק says ״וְאִם הָמֵר יָמִיר״, and the רבנן learn the woman from that extra ״וְ״.

phrases.english: and רבי יהודה does not expound "and if."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן דָּרְשִׁי מִ״וְּאִם״, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה ״וְאִם״ לָא דָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hidden question raised by step 17: what source do the רבנן use for the woman?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different source for the same law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן seem to have no source for including a woman, because they used ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ for the heir.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן learn the woman from ״וְאִם״. רבי יהודה does not expound ״וְאִם״, so he uses ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ for the woman.

steps.title: The משנה lists who does not do סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that everyone does סמיכה on his offering, except a deaf-mute, an imbecile, a minor, a blind person, a גוי, a slave, an agent, and a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Everyone places hands on the offering, except a deaf-mute, an imbecile, a minor, a blind person, a גוי, a slave, an agent, and a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the general rule that everyone does סמיכה, then lists the people who do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is made of exceptions to the rule that every owner of an animal offering does סמיכה. Each exception will need its own reason or source in the גמרא that follows. The agent is excluded because only the owner does סמיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: They place hands, leaning on the animal's head before it is slaughtered.
A deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor. These are people not held responsible for מצוות.
An agent who brings the offering for its owner.
A blind person

phrases.english: MISHNA: Everyone places hands,
except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
and a blind person, a gentile, and a slave,
and the agent, and a woman.
phrases.notes: The agent is the person bringing the offering for its owner. Only the owner himself does סמיכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַכֹּל סוֹמְכִין, חוּץ מֵחֵרֵשׁ, שׁוֹטֶה, וְקָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the end of the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every owner does סמיכה except a deaf-mute, an imbecile, a minor, a blind person, a גוי, a slave, an agent, and a woman.

steps.title: סמיכה is not essential to the offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that סמיכה is a 'leftover' part of the מצוה. Leaving it out does not stop the offering from working.
steps.simpleTranslation: And סמיכה is a non-essential part of the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second rule: סמיכה is a מצוה, but it is not essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling סמיכה ״שְׁיָרֵי מִצְוָה״ means it is an extra part of the מצוה. If the owner did not do סמיכה, the offering still brings atonement. This does not make סמיכה optional; it is still a מצוה to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'leftovers' of a מצוה. These are parts of the מצוה that are not essential to it.
Placing hands on the head of an offering

steps.confusionAlert: ״שְׁיָרֵי מִצְוָה״ does not mean סמיכה is unimportant or optional. It is still a מצוה. It only means the offering still brings atonement if it was not done.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains why a person who could not do סמיכה, such as someone in the משנה's list, can still bring an offering that brings atonement.

phrases.english: And placing hands is a non-essential part of the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling in the same משנה, about the status of סמיכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סמיכה is a non-essential part of the מצוה. Not doing it does not stop the owner from getting atonement.

steps.title: How and where סמיכה is done
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its rules: סמיכה is on the head with both hands, in the place of slaughter, and the שחיטה comes right after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leaning is on the head, with two hands. In the place where they lean, they slaughter. Right after the leaning comes the slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its description of סמיכה. It tells us how it is done (both hands on the head), where it is done (where the animal is slaughtered), and when the שחיטה must happen (right after).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 told us that סמיכה is not required for the offering to work. Now the משנה gives the proper way to do it anyway. It adds three details: body part (head), method (two hands), and place and timing (same spot as the שחיטה, with no gap).

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands with force on the head of the offering
With two hands, not just one
Ritual slaughter of the animal
The slaughter comes immediately after the leaning, with no break

steps.whatToRemember: סמיכה: on the head, with both hands, in the slaughtering place, and the שחיטה follows right away.

phrases.english: On the head, with two hands.
And in the place where they lean, they slaughter.
And immediately after the leaning comes the slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from who does סמיכה and its status to how it is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סמיכה is done on the head with both hands, in the place of slaughter, and the שחיטה follows right after it.

steps.title: Why is a blind person left out of סמיכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the reasons for leaving out the deaf-mute, imbecile, minor and גוי, but asks what the source is for leaving out a סומא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The deaf-mute, the imbecile and the minor make sense, because they do not have proper understanding. The גוי also makes sense, because the פסוק says 'the children of Israel' lean, so non-Jews do not lean. But a blind person — why can he not lean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts on the list of people the משנה (step 19) left out of סמיכה. It says most of them are easy to explain, but the blind person needs a source. This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two clear reasons for most of the list. A חרש, שוטה and קטן lack understanding. A גוי is left out by the words 'בני ישראל'. A blind person has full understanding and is Jewish, so neither reason covers him, and the גמרא asks for his source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It makes sense that…' — we accept this part, but there is a problem with another part
People with proper understanding
A blind person

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It makes sense for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
since they are not people of understanding.
A גוי also makes sense —
"The children of Israel" lean,
but non-Jews do not lean.
But a blind person — what is the reason he does not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה, going back to the list of excluded people from step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source or reason excludes a blind person from סמיכה, since neither lack of understanding nor 'בני ישראל' applies to him?

steps.title: First answer: learned from the Elders of the congregation
steps.stepSummary: One אמורא learns the blind person's exclusion by linking the word סמיכה to the סמיכה done by the זקני העדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רב יצחק בר אבדימי give two answers. One says: we learn 'leaning' from 'leaning' said about the Elders of the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question. The first answer links the סמיכה of a regular offering to the סמיכה done by the זקני העדה, the judges of the סנהדרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזירה שוה, where the same word in two places links their laws. The זקני העדה do סמיכה on a communal offering, and judges may not be blind. So a blind person is left out of every סמיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It comes' — this is learned from another source
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two places
The Elders of the congregation — the judges of the סנהדרין

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי,
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda and Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi:
One said:
It is learned 'leaning' from 'leaning'
from "the Elders of the congregation."

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: אָתְיָא סְמִיכָה סְמִיכָה מִ״זִּקְנֵי עֵדָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the זקני העדה: like the judges, who may not be blind, a blind person cannot do סמיכה.

steps.title: Second answer: learned from the עולת ראייה
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא learns the blind person's exclusion by linking the word סמיכה to the סמיכה on the festival עולת ראייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one says: we learn 'leaning' from 'leaning' said about the burnt offering of appearance.
steps.whatsHappening: The second אמורא gives a different source for the same law. He links regular סמיכה to the סמיכה on the עולת ראייה, the offering brought when coming up to Jerusalem for the festivals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blind person is exempt from the מצוה of coming up for the festivals and bringing the עולת ראייה. Through the same word 'סמיכה', the second אמורא carries that exemption over to all סמיכה. Both answers agree on the law; they only argue about which source it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The burnt offering brought when 'appearing' in Jerusalem on the festivals

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees a blind person does not do סמיכה. The argument is only about the source: the זקני העדה or the עולת ראייה.
steps.confusionAlert: These two אמוראים do not argue about the law itself. They agree a blind person is left out and only differ about where we learn it from.

phrases.english: And the other one said:
It is learned 'leaning' from 'leaning'
from the burnt offering of appearance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: אָתְיָא סְמִיכָה סְמִיכָה מֵעוֹלַת רְאִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different source for the same answer to step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the עולת ראייה: a blind person is exempt from that offering, so he is also left out of סמיכה.

steps.title: Why not learn from the Elders of the congregation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the אמורא who learns from עולת ראייה why he does not learn from the זקני העדה instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who said we learn it from the festival burnt offering, what is the reason he does not learn it from the Elders of the congregation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the second אמורא why he did not use the first אמורא's source. This sets up an answer that will show a weakness in learning from the זקני העדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים agree that a סומא is excluded from סמיכה. They only disagree about the source. The גמרא wants to know what is wrong with the זקני העדה source in the eyes of the one who chose עולת ראייה.

keyTerms.meaning: The burnt offering brought when a person comes to the בית המקדש on a festival
The Elders of the congregation, who do סמיכה on the bull brought when the community sins by mistake
He learns (derives)
What is the reason?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge against the הלכה. Everyone agrees a סומא does not do סמיכה. The question is only why this אמורא chose one source over the other.

phrases.english: And according to the one who said from the burnt offering of appearance,
phrases.notes: This is the second אמורא from the last step, who links the word סמיכה to the festival offering.

phrases.english: what is the reason he does not derive it
from the Elders of the congregation?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר מֵעוֹלַת רְאִיָּיה, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא יָלֵיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the second אמורא from step 24 why he rejects the source of the first אמורא from step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What weakness this אמורא sees in learning the blind person's exclusion from the סמיכה of the זקני העדה.
